claim: Governed delegation joins an assignment to relevant knowledge, durable work, and acceptance evidence. Context selection is bounded and advisory. Dispatch gates act on assignment structure and resolved phase state; completion review evaluates landed work and independent evidence. Recovery preserves existing artifacts before work is reassigned.
topology: A work order supplies target scope and declared phase identity. Component and constraint models and target scope feed bounded context selection, which guides an agent but does not enforce every obligation. Lifecycle policy and reconciled observed phase state remain distinct inputs to selected dispatch checks; absence of completion evidence is not a positive DONE match. The implementing agent preserves durable artifacts. Completion review evaluates landed work and independent evidence before recording acceptance. Interrupted or unresolved work is inspected before reassignment.
bw_encoding: Rectangles identify models and artifacts; rounded boxes identify mechanisms, and diamonds mark admission decisions. Gray identifies flexible reasoning only. Heavy outlines mark consequential application/admission boundaries. Solid arrows carry data, models or results; dashed arrows carry verification/challenge or subordinate selection relations.
redesign: Author-approved model-centered appendix revision: two new compact architecture figures aligned with settled five-model inventories, plus targeted model-role clarifications in the existing mutation and delegation figures.
